||I did not live as I should have. My lady would have me work the land and protect my neighbor. I should have lived a life of merriment to spread joy to others who grieve. But I am not that man, nor will I live to be him. So I will fight. But should you read this that I fell, do not grieve for me. Do not grieve the man who would harm others to restore his own grievance. Do not grieve the fool who would give you a false hope. Shed no tears for old and weary for he has chosen to walk this road.

But I will not fight for simply death. I do not love my axe for that which falls. I do not love the struggle to curry glory or honor. I do not love the pain that torments my waking and dreaming thoughts. But should I fall, carry on.||

||carry on for the markets and the new lands. Carry on for the simple pleasures of life and kinship of others. I do not fight for myself, but for the smiles of many others that I never had the heart to have. I fight that others may carry in without the fear that I have carried under a black sun and centuries. I fight for love, I fight for freedom, I fight for chauntea. I am your shield, and the joy of a shield is to be beaten and broken to protect the bearer.||
